title: OverlayMarks
description: Ground truth for one overlay eval case: the moments in a reference video's narration where a graphic SHOULD appear, where one should NOT, and where the reference did something this pipeline cannot express. Authored by a human from a reference video using docs/10-overlay-marks.md; consumed only by the scorer in worker/lusora_worker/evals/overlays.py. It is a judgement, never an artifact — nothing in the production pipeline reads it.

case.description: Matches the case directory name under evals/overlays/. A leading underscore marks a case that is not a reference video — _synthetic is the scorer's own fixture.

level.description: How much of the reference the author actually saw, on docs/09-video-teardown.md's scale. L1 (transcript only) cannot honestly mark component choice; L2+ can.

source.description: Provenance. Absent on a synthetic case, which has no reference.

source_words.description: A verbatim, contiguous span of the case's script.txt — how a mark finds its beat. Never a timestamp: the case's script is narrated by OUR TTS, so the reference video's timings do not transfer. The span must occur EXACTLY ONCE in the script; the scorer treats zero or two occurrences as a fixture bug and refuses to score.

at.description: Reference-video timestamp the mark was taken from. For a human re-checking the mark against the source; the scorer ignores it.

verdict.description: graphic = a graphic belongs here. no_graphic = it does not, and placing one costs restraint. unmappable = the reference did something this pipeline has no field for, so the moment is excluded from every score rather than counted as a miss.

class.description: graphic only. The two reasons an overlay may exist (the Overlay Rule): it carries a fact the narration says, or it is pure text lifting a moment. They are separately budgeted (D59), so the ground truth has to say which.

acceptable.description: graphic only. Every catalog component that would be a defensible choice here. More than one is normal and is the point: component_accuracy asks whether the planner chose defensibly, not whether it read the author's mind.

ideal.description: graphic only. The best of `acceptable`, and MUST be a member of it — the scorer rejects a case where it is not. Recorded for reading results, not scored on its own.

near_miss.description: no_graphic only. This span DOES contain an anchor of this type — a legal, gate-passing place to put a graphic — and the answer is still no. The field that separates a discriminating negative from a trivial one: a restraint score built only on spans with no anchor in them measures nothing, because the anchor gate already refuses those.

excluded_from_scoring.description: unmappable only, and required there. Written out rather than inferred so that reading the file tells you a moment was dropped on purpose.

why.description: The reason, in the author's words. Unscored, and the most useful field in the file when a score moves and nobody can remember why the mark says what it says.
